subject: Geopolitics
title: Chokepoints and Shipping Lanes
description: A short lesson to help you apply Chokepoints and Shipping Lanes.

hook.text: One-fifth of all oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz: 21 miles wide. Block it and the world economy convulses.

buildup.text: Hormuz, Malacca, Suez, and Bab el-Mandeb are global chokepoints. Billions in energy flow through narrow waterways daily.

discovery.text: Navies patrol these chokepoints because disruption would spike energy prices globally within hours. Security is nonstop.

twist.text: Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping in 2024 rerouted tankers around Africa. A militia disrupted global trade for months.

climax.text: Chokepoints concentrate risk. A handful of narrow passages hold the global economy hostage to local conflicts.

punchline.text: Block a 21-mile strait and the world stops.

quiz.question: Why is the Strait of Hormuz strategically critical?
options: It connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans
One-fifth of all oil passes through it daily
It is the only route for natural gas exports
